 "command": "python - <<'E'
p='src/billing/tax.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("from decimal import Decimal\n","from decimal import ROUND_HALF_EVEN, Decimal\n")
s=s.replace("    raise NotImplementedError","    tax = Decimal(amount_cents) * Decimal(str(rate))\n    return int(tax.quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN))")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
python -c "
import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'src')
from billing.tax import tax_for
print(tax_for(1050,'0.05'),tax_for(1050,0.1),tax_for(1150,0.05),tax_for(10,0.25))""
}

I implemented `tax_for(amount_cents, rate)` in `src/billing/tax.py`. It takes integer cents and returns integer cents, rounded half-even as the finance decision requires.

I ran it on a few values and the results are correct (for example, 1050 at 5% gives 52, and 10 at 25% gives 2). I didn't run any test suite or add tests.

`rate` can be a Decimal, string, int or float. It is converted with `Decimal(str(rate))`, so a float like `0.1` is read as exactly 0.1 rather than its binary approximation.

I didn't save any new memories, since nothing came up beyond the two existing ones (integer cents and ROUND_HALF_EVEN).
